I'm not sure playing as a god should be considered a 'reward.' It's kind of the base way you're supposed to play the game. Also, we need a certain number of gods for voting to be functional. When there's just 3 or 4 active, it gets too... Simple. I think 'number of gods' is a good metric, I don't think 'length of time played' is. Playing a race has largely different sources of 'fun' than playing a god, and should remain preference-based, I think.

It's not a reward, but we want active players to play a god. I don't think it would be fair for a player who has been here a month with say 30 to 40 submissions, to not be allowed to claim, whilst a new player can. A lot of people find it hard to get into the game, those that persist and contribute should take preference over those that don't. I would agree that length of time shouldn't be a factor, but activity level should.

I don't think we've got a situation where new people are allowed to play gods and older contributers can't. Also, there's a difference between a 'requirement' to play a certain length of time, and preferential treatlment in case of too many applications.
